##### 2.6.7.5 ModifyDiskReplicaPair

Modifies the name, RPO, or description of a replication pair.

**Usage notes**

The replication pair must be in the **created** or **stopped** state. After a replication pair is added to a replication pair-consistent group, you cannot directly modify the RPO of the replication pair.

**Request headers**

This operation uses only common request headers. For more information, see Common request headers.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Positi on | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RegionId | Strin g | Quer y | Yes | cn-beijing | The region ID of the replication pair. This is the region of the primary site. |

| ReplicaPair Id | Strin g | Quer y | Yes | pair-cn-dsa**** | The replication pair ID. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PairName | Strin g | Quer y | No | TestReplicaPair | The replication pair name. |

##### 2.6.7.7 ReprotectDiskReplicaPair

Enables the reverse replication feature for a replication pair. After you enable the reverse replication feature, the direction of data replication is inverted. Data is replicated from the original secondary disk to the original primary disk.

**Usage notes**

The replication pair must be in the **failovered**, **reprotecting**, or **reprotect_failed** state and is not added to any replication pair-consistent group. The primary disk must be detached from its associated ECS instance and is in the Unattached state. You can call the DetachDisk operation to detach disks. After you enable the reverse replication feature, you must call the StartDiskReplicaPair operation again to enable the replication pair before data can be replicated from the original secondary disk to the original primary disk.

**Request headers**

This operation uses only common request headers. For more information, see Common request headers.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ClientToke n | Strin g | Quer y | No | 123e4567-e89b-12d3- a456-426655440000 | The client token that is used to ensure the idempotence of the request. You can use the client to generate the value, but make sure that the value is unique among different requests. The ClientToken value can contain only ASCII characters and cannot exceed 64 characters in length. For more information, see How to ensure idempotence. |

|---|---|---|---|

##### 2.6.7.8 StopDiskReplicaPair

Stops a replication pair.

**Methods**

The replication pair must be in the **initial_syncing**, **manual_syncing**, **syncing**, **normal**,
**stopping**, **stopping_failed**, or **stopped** state and not be added to any replication pair-
consistent group. After you stop a replication pair, the replication pair enters the **stopped** state. The secondary disk rolls back to the point in time when the last asynchronous replication was complete and drops all the data that is being replicated from the primary disk. If you stop a replication pair that is in the **initial_syncing** state and then perform a failover, an error is returned.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Requir ed | Example | Description |

| Action | String | Yes | StopDiskReplica Pair | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to StopDiskReplicaPair. |

| ReplicaPairId | String | Yes | pair-cn-dsa**** | The ID of the replication pair. |

| ClientToken | String | No | 123e4567-e89b- 12d3-a456- 426655440000 | The client token that is used to ensure the idempotence of the request. You can use the client to generate the value, but make sure that the value is unique among different requests. The ClientToken value can contain only ASCII characters and cannot exceed 64 characters in length. For more information, see How to ensure idempotence. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

##### 2.6.7.9 DeleteDiskReplicaPair

Deletes a replication pair.

**Usage notes**

The replication pair must be in the **creating**, **created**, **create_failed**, **stopped**,
**failovered**, **deleting**, **delete_failed**, or **invalid** state. This operation deletes only
replication pairs. The primary and secondary disks in the deleted replication pairs are retained. To delete a replication pair, you must call this operation in the region in which the primary disk is located. After the replication pair is deleted, functionality limits are lifted from the primary and secondary disks. For example, you can attach the secondary disk, resize the disk, or read data from or write data to the disk. The request initiated by calling this operation is successful even if you specify a replication pair ID that does not exist or is invalid.

**Request parameters**

You can use the client to generate the token, but you must make sure that the token is unique among different requests. #### 2.6.8 Replication pair-consistent groups

##### 2.6.8.1 CreateDiskReplicaGroup

Creates a replication pair-consistent group.

**Usage notes**

A replication pair-consistent group is a combination of multiple replication pairs that replicate data in the same direction. A replication pair-consistent group allows you to start or stop multiple replication pairs, perform failovers for multiple replication pairs, or enable the reverse replication feature for multiple replication pairs at a time. When you create a replication pair-consistent group, take note of the following items: Replication pair-consistent groups support disaster recovery across zones within the same region. A replication pair and a replication pair-consistent group replicate in the same direction if they have the same primary region (production region), primary zone (production zone), secondary region (disaster recovery region), and secondary zone (disaster recovery zone). Replication pairs can be added only to a replication pair-consistent group that replicates in the same direction as them. After replication pairs are added to a replication pair-consistent group, the recovery point objective (RPO) of the group takes effect on the replication pairs in place of their original RPOs.

**Request headers**

This operation uses only common request headers. For more information, see Common request headers.

##### 2.6.8.2 AddDiskReplicaPair

Adds a replication pair to a replication pair-consistent group.

**Usage notes**

A replication pair and a replication pair-consistent group replicate data in the same direction if they have the same primary region (production region), primary zone (production zone), secondary region (disaster recovery region), and secondary zone (disaster recovery zone). A replication pair can be added to a replication pair-consistent group only when they replicate data in the same direction. A maximum of 512 replication pairs can be added to a replication pair-consistent group. Before you add a replication pair to a replication pair-consistent group, make sure that the pair and the group are in the **created** or **stopped** state.

##### 2.6.8.3 StartDiskReplicaGroup

Enables the asynchronous replication feature for the replication pairs in a replication pairconsistent group. After you enable the asynchronous replication feature, the system first performs a full synchronization to synchronize all data from the primary disks to the secondary disks and then periodically synchronizes incremental data based on the RPO of the replication pair-consistent group.

**Usage notes**

If you want to perform automatic synchronization by setting the OneShot parameter to false, make sure that the replication pair-consistent group is in the **created**, **syncing**,
**normal**, or **stopped** state.
If you want to perform manual synchronization by setting the OneShot parameter to true, make sure the replication pair-consistent group is in the **created**, **manual_syncing**, or
**stopped** state.
After you enable the asynchronous replication feature for a replication pair-consistent group, the group enters the **initial_syncing** state. The system performs the first asynchronous replication to replicate all data from the primary disks to the secondary disks.

**Request headers**

This operation uses only common request headers. For more information, see Common request headers.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Positi on | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RegionId | Strin g | Quer y | Yes | cn-beijing | The region ID of the primary disks or secondary disks in the replication pair-consistent group. The value of this parameter is also the identifier and a component of Endpoint, as shown in the following sample request. |
| ReplicaGro upId | Strin g | Quer y | Yes | pg-myreplica**** | The ID of the replication pair-consistent group. |

| ClientToke n | Strin g | Quer y | No | 123e4567-e89b-12d3- a456-426655440000 | The client token that is used to ensure the idempotence of the request. You can use the client to generate the value, but make sure that the value is unique among different requests. The ClientToken value can contain only ASCII characters and cannot exceed 64 characters in length. For more information, see How to ensure idempotence. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OneShot | Bool ean | Quer y | No | true | Specifies whether to immediately synchronize data. Valid values: true: immediately synchronizes data. false (default): synchronizes data based on the RPO of the replication pair- consistent group. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | C123F94F-4E38- 19AE-942A- A8D6F44F0450 | The ID of the request. |

##### 2.6.8.4 DescribeDiskReplicaGroups

Queries the information of one or more replication pair-consistent groups in a region.

**Usage notes**

You can use one of the following methods to check the responses: Method 1: Use NextToken to configure the query token. Set the value to the NextToken value returned in the last call to the operation. Then, use MaxResults to specify the maximum number of entries to return on each page. Method 2: Use PageSize to specify the number of entries to return on each page and then use PageNumber to specify the page number to return. You can use only one of the preceding methods. If you require a large number of entries to be returned, we recommend that you use method 1. When NextToken is specified, the PageSize and PageNumber request parameters do not take effect and the TotalCount response parameter is invalid.

##### 2.6.8.6 FailoverDiskReplicaGroup

Enables the failover feature for the replication pairs in a replication pair-consistent group. When the primary disks of specific replication pairs in a replication pair-consistent group fail, you can call this operation to grant the read and write permissions on the secondary disks.

**Usage notes**

The replication pair-consistent group must be in the **manual_syncing**, **syncing**, **normal**,
**stopping**, **stop_failed**, **stopped**, **failovering**, **failover_failed**, or **failovered** state.
After a failover is performed, the replication pair-consistent group enters the **failovered** state. Before you perform a failover, make sure that the first full data synchronization is complete between the primary site and the secondary site.

**Request headers**

This operation uses only common request headers. For more information, see Common request headers.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| ClientToke n | Strin g | Quer y | No | 123e4567-e89b-12d3- a456-426655440000 | The client token that is used to ensure the idempotence of the request. You can use the client to generate the token, but you must make sure that the token is unique among different requests. The token can contain only ASCII characters and cannot exceed 64 characters in length. For more information, see How to ensure idempotence. |

##### 2.6.8.7 ReprotectDiskReplicaGroup

Enables the reverse replication feature for the replication pairs in a replication pair-consistent group. After you enable the reverse replication feature, the direction of data replication is reversed. Data is replicated from the original secondary disks to the original primary disks.

**Usage notes**

The replication pair-consistent group for which you want to enable the reverse replication feature must be in the **failovered** state. You can call the FailoverDiskReplicaPair operation to enable the failover feature. The primary disk must be detached from its associated Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance and is in the Unattached state. You can call the DetachDisk operation to detach disks. After you enable the reverse replication feature, you must call the StartDiskReplicaPairGroup operation again to enable the asynchronous replication feature for the replication pairs in a replication pair-consistent group before data can be replicated from the original secondary disk to the original primary disk.

**Request headers**

This operation uses only common request headers. For more information, see Common request headers.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| ReplicaGr oupId | Strin g | Query | Yes | pg-myreplica**** | The replication pair- consistent group ID. |
| ClientToke n | Strin g | Query | No | 123e4567-e89b-12d3- a456-426655440000 | The client token that is used to ensure the idempotence of the request. You can use the client to generate the token, but you must make sure that the token is unique among different requests. The token can contain only ASCII characters and cannot exceed 64 characters in length. For more information, see How to ensure idempotence. |
| SourceRe gionId | Strin g | Query | No | cn-beijing | This parameter is unavailable. |
| SourceZon eId | Strin g | Query | No | cn-beijing-f | This parameter is unavailable. |

##### 2.6.8.8 ReprotectDiskReplicaPair

Enables the reverse replication feature for a replication pair. After you enable the reverse replication feature, the direction of data replication is inverted. Data is replicated from the original secondary disk to the original primary disk.

**Usage notes**

The replication pair must be in the **failovered**, **reprotecting**, or **reprotect_failed** state and is not added to a replication pair-consistent group. The primary disk must be detached from the associated ECS instance and is in the Unattached state. You can call the DetachDisk operation to detach disks. After you enable the reverse replication feature, you must call the StartDiskReplicaPair operation again to activate the async replication feature before data can be replicated from the original secondary disk to the original primary disk. You can also configure the ReverseReplicate parameter to cancel the failovered state.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common headers" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Loca tion | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RegionId | Strin g | Quer y | Yes | cn-shanghai | The region ID of the secondary disk in the replication pair. You can call the DescribeDiskReplicaPairs operation to obtain the region information of secondary disks in replication pairs. |
| ReplicaPair Id | Strin g | Quer y | Yes | pair-cn-dsa**** | The ID of the replication pair. |
| ClientToke n | Strin g | Quer y | No | 123e4567-e89b-12d3- a456-426655440000 | The client token that is used to ensure the idempotency of the request. You can use the client to generate the token, but you must make sure that the token is unique among different requests. The token contains only ASCII characters and cannot exceed 64 characters in length. For more information, see How to ensure idempotence. |

| ReverseRe plicate | Bool ean | Quer y | No | false | Specifies whether to enable the reverse replication feature. Valid values: true and false. Default value: true. A value of true indicates that the reverse replication feature is enabled. A value of false indicates that the reverse replication feature is disabled and the failovered state of a replication pair is canceled. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | C123F94F-4E38- 19AE-942A- A8D6F44F0450 | The ID of the request. |

##### 2.6.8.10 StopDiskReplicaGroup

Disables the asynchronous replication feature for the replication pairs in a replication pairconsistent group.

**Usage notes**

The replication pair-consistent group must be in the **manual_syncing**, **syncing**, **normal**,
**stopping**, **stop_failed**, or **stopped** state.
After the asynchronous replication feature is disabled for a replication pair-consistent group, the group enters the **stopped** state. If the asynchronous replication feature cannot be disabled, the state of the group remains unchanged or changes to **stop_failed**. In this case, try again later.

You can use the client to generate the token, but you must make sure that the token is unique among different requests. #### 2.6.10 Appendix

##### 2.6.10.1 How to ensure idempotence

If a request timeout or an internal server error occurs when you call an EBS API operation, the client may resend the request. In this case, you can set the **ClientToken** parameter in the request to prevent the client from repeatedly sending the request.

**What is idempotence**

Idempotence is a property of some operations and resources in mathematics and computer science. Idempotence allows you to obtain the result of the initial request after a request is resent multiple times. Idempotence plays an important role in the distributed system design.

**How to ensure idempotence**

In most cases, the client resends a request only when error 500 ( `InternalErrorInternalError` ) or 503 ( `ServiceUnavailable` ) is returned or when no response is received. When you use EBS API, the client generates a parameter value that consists of up to 64 ASCII characters, and you can assign the value to **ClientToken** to ensure the idempotence of the resent requests.

**ClientToken details**

The following section describes the details of **ClientToken**: The **ClientToken** value is a unique and case-sensitive string that is generated by a client and can contain up to 64 ASCII characters in length. Example: `ClientToken=123e4567-e89b-`

```
12d3-a456-426655440000 .
```

If you provide a used value for the **ClientToken** parameter and use different values for other request parameters, the cloud service returns the error code

```
 IdempotentParameterMismatch .
```

> **Note:** You must use different values for **SignatureNonce**, **Timestamp**, and **Signature** in each retry. This is because ECS uses **SignatureNonce** to prevent replay attacks and uses **Timestamp** to identify the timestamp of each request. Therefore, you must specify different **SignatureNonce** and **Timestamp** values in a resent request. Consequently, this changes the value of **Signature**.

After you specify the **ClientToken** parameter in a request, the following results may be returned: If the HTTP status code 200 is returned, the client will receive the same result as the last request after the request is resent. However, your server status will not be affected. If an HTTP status code 4xx is returned without the `try it later` error message, a retry will fail. You must troubleshoot issues based on the returned error message before you resend a request.

**Sample idempotent requests**

In this example, the CreateDisk operation is called to create a cloud disk. If you send multiple requests that use the same **ClientToken** value whereas other request parameters remain unchanged, the server returns identical request results with identical **DiskId** values.

```
https://ecs.example.com/?Action=CreateDisk &RegionId=cn-qingdao-env17-d01 &ZoneId=cn-qingdao-env17-amtest11001-a &SnapshotId=s-bp67acfmxazb4p**** &DiskName=test-DiskName &Size=2000 &DiskCategory=cloud_ssd &Description=This is a description example. &Encrypted=false &ClientToken=123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426655440000 &Tag.1.Key=TestKey &Tag.1.Value=TestValue &<Common request parameters>
```

If you do not use **ClientToken**, multiple cloud disks may be created when the client retries operations after errors occur.

**List of operations**

The following section lists some API operations that include **ClientToken** for your reference. For information about whether an API operation includes **ClientToken**, see the topic that describes the API operation.

##### 2.6.10.2 API operations and states related to a replication pair

**replication pair**

This topic describes the API operations and states related to a replication pair.

**API operations**

| API operation | State |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|
|   | Before the operation | If the operation succeeds | If the operation fails |
| CreateDiskReplicaPair | The replication pair does not exist. | created | The operation returns an error, or the replication pair enters the create failed state. _ |
| StartDiskReplicaPair (Automatic synchronization) | created, initial syncing, or _ stopped | The replication pair is in the initial syncing _ state during the first synchronization. Otherwise, the replication pair is in the syncing state. After the synchronization of the current cycle is complete, the replication pair enters the normal state. | The state remains unchanged. |
|   | syncing or normal | The state remains unchanged. | The state remains unchanged. |
| StartDiskReplicaPair (Manual synchronization) | created, manual syncing, or _ stopped | manual syncing _ | The state remains unchanged. |
| StopDiskReplicaPair | syncing, init syncing, _ manual syncing, _ normal, stopping, stop failed, or stopped _ | stopped | The state remains unchanged or changes to stop failed. _ |

| FailoverDiskReplicaPair | manual syncing, _ syncing, normal, stopping, stop failed, _ stopped, failovering, failover failed, or _ failovered | failovered | failover failed _ |
|---|---|---|---|
| ReprotectDiskReplicaP air | failovered, reprotect failed, or _ reprotecting | stopped | reprotect failed _ |
| DeleteDiskReplicaPair | created, stopped, invalid, deleted, delete failed, or _ deleting | The replication pair does not exist. | delete failed _ |
| ModifyDiskReplicaPair | created or stopped | The state remains unchanged. | The state remains unchanged. |

**States**

| State | Name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| creating | Creating | The replication pair is being created. |
| created | Created | The replication pair is created. |
| create failed _ | Creation Failed | The replication pair cannot be created. We recommend that you delete the replication pair and call the CreateDiskReplicaPair operation again. |
| normal | Normal | The synchronization of the current cycle is complete. |
| initial syncing _ | Initial Syncing | Data is being synchronized for the first time. |
| manual syncing _ | One-time Syncing | After data is manually synchronized from the primary disk to the secondary disk, the replication pair returns to the stopped state. If data is manually synchronized from the primary disk to the secondary disk for the first time, the replication pair is in the manual syncing state _ during the synchronization. |
| syncing | Syncing | Data is being synchronized. |
| invalid | Invalid | The replication pair becomes abnormal due to a user operation. We recommend that you troubleshoot related issues based on the status message. |
| stopping | Stopping | The replication pair is being stopped. |
| stopped | Stopped | The replication pair is stopped. |
| stop failed _ | Stop Failed | The replication pair cannot be stopped. We recommend that you call the StopDiskReplicaPair operation again. |

| deleting | Deleting | The replication pair is being deleted. |
|---|---|---|
| delete failed _ | Deletion Failed | The replication pair cannot be deleted. We recommend that you call the DeleteDiskReplicaPair operation again. |
| deleted | Deleted | The replication pair is deleted. This state is invisible. |
| failovering | In Failover | The failover is being performed. |
| failover failed _ | Failover Failed | The failover cannot be performed. We recommend that you call the FailoverDiskReplicaPair operation again. |
| failovered | Failed Over | The failover is complete. |
| reprotecting | In Reverse Replication | The reverse replication is being performed. |
| reprotect failed _ | Reverse Replication Failed | The reverse replication cannot be performed. We recommend that you call the ReprotectDiskReplicaPair operation again. |

|---|---|---|
| creating | Creating | The replication pair-consistent group is being created. |
| created | Created | The replication pair-consistent group is created. |
| create failed _ | Creation Failed | The replication pair-consistent group cannot be created. We recommend that you delete the replication pair-consistent group and call the CreateDiskReplicaGroup operation again. |
| normal | Normal | The synchronization of the current cycle is complete. |
| manual syncing _ | One-time Syncing | After data is manually synchronized from the primary disks to the secondary disks, the replication pair-consistent group returns to the stopped state. If data is manually synchronized from the primary disks to the secondary disks for the first time, the replication pair-consistent group is in the manual syncing state during the synchronization. _ |
| syncing | Syncing | Data is being synchronized. |
| invalid | Invalid | The replication pair-consistent group becomes abnormal due to a user operation. We recommend that you troubleshoot related issues based on the status message. |

| stopping | Stopping | The replication pair-consistent group is being stopped. |
|---|---|---|
| stopped | Stopped | The replication pair-consistent group is stopped. |
| stop failed _ | Stop Failed | The replication pair-consistent group cannot be stopped. We recommend that you call the StopDiskReplicaGroup operation again. |
| deleting | Deleting | The replication pair-consistent group is being deleted. |
| delete failed _ | Deletion Failed | The replication pair-consistent group cannot be deleted. We recommend that you call the DeleteDiskReplicaGroup operation again. Before you can delete a replication pair- consistent group, make sure that no replication pairs are present in the group. |
| deleted | Deleted | The replication pair-consistent group is deleted. This state is not visible. |
| failovering | In Failover | The failover is being performed. |
| failover failed _ | Failover Failed | The failover cannot be performed. We recommend that you call the FailoverDiskReplicaGroup operation again. |
| failovered | Failed Over | The failover is complete. |
| reprotecting | In Reverse Replication | The reverse replication is being performed. |
| reprotect failed _ | Reverse Replication Failed | The reverse replication cannot be performed. We recommend that you call the ReprotectDiskReplicaGroup operation again. |

## 3 Log Service

### 3.1 Preparations

#### 3.1.1 Obtain an AccessKey pair

AccessKey pairs can be assigned by Resource Access Management (RAM). You must use the type of AccessKey pairs for authentication when you call API operations. This topic describes how to obtain an AccessKey pair that is assigned by RAM.

**Background information**

An AccessKey pair is used to verify the identity of a request sender based on symmetric encryption. An AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. The AccessKey ID is used to identify a user. The AccessKey secret is used to encrypt the signature string. You can use RAM to assign an AccessKey pair that consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret to a third party for authentication.

> **Warning:** The AccessKey pair of a personal account is managed and limited by the permission system of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. If you need to obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization, make sure that your operation is allowed by an administrator. This ensures security.

**Obtain the AccessKey pair of a personal account**

To obtain the AccessKey pair of a personal account, perform the following operations:
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the upper-right corner of the page that appears, click the profile picture, and then click
**User Information**.
3. In the **AccessKey Pair** section, view the AccessKey pair of your account.

> **Note:** An AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. These credentials provide full permissions on cloud resources within your account. You must keep the AccessKey pair confidential.

**Obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization**

To obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization, perform the following operations:
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an administrator.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Resources > Organizations**.
4. In the organization list, click the name of the level-1 organization whose AccessKey pair you
want to obtain.
5. Click **Management Accesskey**.
6. In the dialog box that appears, view the AccessKey pair of the organization.

#### 3.1.2 Obtain the endpoint of Simple Log Service

**Service**

This topic describes how to obtain the endpoint of Simple Log Service.

**Background information**

When you call Apsara Stack operations, endpoints are used. You can obtain an endpoint from onsite Alibaba Cloud O&M engineers. You can also perform the following operations to obtain an endpoint.

**Method 1: Obtain the endpoint in the Apsara Uni-manager**

**Operations console**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Platform Operation > Apsara Infrastructure**
**Management > O&M Tools**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **O&M ToolsService Registration Variable**
**Dashboard**.
4. On the **Service Registration Variable Dashboard** page, enter sls in the search box.
5. In the search results, find sls-backend-server and click the value in the Service Registration
column.
6. In the **Registration Variables** dialog box, obtain the endpoint.
View the value of the **sls_data.endpoint** variable. The value indicates the `endpoint` of Simple Log Service. In most cases, the endpoint of Simple Log Service is in the

```
 data.${global:region}.sls-pub.${global:internet-domain}  format.
```

**Method 2: Obtain the endpoint in the Simple Log Service**

**console**

After you create a project, you can view the endpoint of the project on the Project Overview page.
1. Log on to the Simple Log Service console.
2. In the Projects section, click the project that you want to manage.
3. On the **Project Overview** page, view the endpoint of the project.
View the value of the Private Endpoint parameter. The endpoint of Simple Log Service is in the data.${global:region}.sls-pub.${global:internet-domain} format.

#### 3.1.3 Obtain Simple Log Service SDK

When you call Apsara Stack operations, you must use the SDK of your cloud service. This topic describes how to obtain Alibaba Cloud SDKs. An SDK includes code and examples. You can create cloud applications by using an SDK for the programming language that you require. SDKs for Java, Python, and Go are provided. You can obtain an SDK from Alibaba Cloud SDKs based on your business requirements.

> **Note:** We recommend that you use an SDK for Java, Python, or Go. If you use SDKs for other programming languages, the SDKs may be incompatible with your system.

We recommend that you use the SDK core library that is provided on the Alibaba Cloud official website. The SDK core library is shared by all cloud services and is compatible with Apsara Stack. The following table provides GitHub links to the source code of Simple Log Service SDK for common programming languages.

| SDK programming language | GitHub link |

| Java | Log Service Java SDK |
| Python | Log Service Python SDK |
| Go | Log Service Go SDK |
| PHP | Log Service PHP SDK |

### 3.2 SDK Reference

#### 3.2.1 Introduction

##### 3.2.1.1 Overview

Log Service provide software development kits (SDKs) for multiple languages, such as Java, .NET, Python, PHP, and C. You can select an SDK based on your business requirements. Log Service SDKs are implemented based on Log Service APIs. Log Service SDKs provide the same capabilities as Log Service APIs. For more information about Log Service APIs, see API Reference. Before you can use a Log Service SDK, you must have an active Alibaba Cloud AccessKey pair (AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret). In addition, you must specify the endpoint of Log Service in the SDK. For more information, see Basic configurations. Log Service SDKs can be regarded as Log Service APIs that are encapsulated in different languages to provide the following features: Uniform encapsulation. Log Service APIs are uniformly encapsulated. You do not need to create API requests and parse API responses. For more information, see API specifications. The APIs in different languages are similar. This simplifies the switchover between different languages. Automatic digital signatures. You do not need to specify the digital signature logic of Log Service APIs. This simplifies the use of Log Service APIs. Protocol Buffer-formatted encapsulation. The logs collected by Log Service are encapsulated in the Protocol Buffer format. You do not need to specify the format. Automatic compression. Logs are compressed by using the method defined in Log Service APIs. You do not need to manually compress logs. SDKs in some languages allow you to specify whether to write logs in the compression mode. The compression mode is used by default. Centralized error handling methods. You can use SDKs to handle errors based on the relevant language. For more information, see Error handling. Synchronous requests. SDKs in all languages support only synchronous requests. The following table describes the download address and user guide of Log Service SDKs in different languages.

| SDK language | Documentation | Source code |
|---|---|---|
| Java | Java SDK and Log Service SDK for Java 0.6.0 API | GitHub |
| .NET | .NET SDK and Aliyun.Api.SLS Namespace | GitHub |
| PHP | PHP SDK and SLS PHP SDK _ _ | GitHub |
| Node.js | Node.js SDK | GitHub |
| Python | Python SDK and Python documentation | GitHub |
| C | SDK for C | GitHub |
| GO | SDK for Go | GitHub |
| iOS | iOS SDK | GitHub |
| Android | SDK for Android | GitHub |

| C++ | SDK for C ++ | GitHub |
|---|---|---|

##### 3.2.1.2 Basic configurations

Before you can use SDKs to interact with Log Service, you must configure the basic settings. This topic describes the basic SDK configurations. Basic configurations: Endpoint: You must specify the endpoint that is used by the client to access Log Service. AccessKey pair (AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret): You must specify the AccessKey pair that is used by the client to access Log Service. The following sections describe how to use endpoints and AccessKey pairs.

**Endpoint**

Before you use an SDK, you must determine the access method and endpoint.
1. When you select an endpoint for a client instance, make sure that the region of your project
is the same as the region of your endpoint. Otherwise, you cannot use the SDK to access your project.
2. All API endpoints support only the HTTP protocol.

**AccessKey pairs**

All interaction requests that are sent to Log Service must be authenticated. An AccessKey pair that consists of an AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret is the critical factor for the authentication. When you create a client instance, you must specify an AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret. You must obtain an AccessKey pair in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

> **Note:** An Apsara Stack tenant account can have multiple AccessKey pairs. You must specify the AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret of the same AccessKey pair when you create a client instance. Otherwise, authentication fails.
> The specified AccessKey must be in the Enabled state. Otherwise, the requests are denied by Log Service. To view the status of the AccessKey pair, you can log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Examples**

Assume that you want to access a project and you have an AccessKey pair that is in the Enabled state. The following AccessKey pair is used:

```
AccessKeyId = "<yourAccessKeyId>" AccessKeySecret = "<yourAccessKeySecret>"
```


##### 3.2.1.3 Error handling

This topic describes the basic error handling. SDK errors are classified into the following types: Errors returned by Log Service. This type of errors are handled by SDKs. For more information about this type of errors, see the common error codes of the Log Service API operations. Network errors that occur when you use SDKs to send requests to the server. This type of errors include network disconnection and server response timeout. Errors that are generated by SDKs and are related to platforms or programming languages, for example, memory overflows. All SDKs that are provided by Alibaba Cloud handle errors by throwing exceptions based on the following rules: If the first or second types of errors occur, the SDKs encapsulate the errors as the LogException class and then send the class to users. If the third type of errors occur, the SDKs do not handle the errors but send the errors as the platform-specific and language-specific NativeException class to users.

**LogException**

The LogException class is defined by SDKs to handle the logical errors of Log Service. This class inherits the base class for all exceptions from each language, and provides the following exception information: Error code: indicates the error type. For an error returned by Log Service when you use an SDK, the error code is the same as the error code that is returned by the relevant API operation. The error code for network request errors of SDKs is RequestError. For more information, see API Reference. Error message: indicates the message that is returned together with an error. For an error returned by Log Service when you use an SDK, the error message is the same as the error code that is returned by the relevant API operation. The error message of network errors is "request is failed". For more information, see API Reference. Request ID: indicates the ID of the request for which the current error is returned. The request ID is generated by Log Service. The request ID is returned only when Log Service returns an error message. If Log Service does not return an error message, an empty string is returned. If you receive a request error, you can provide the relevant request ID to the Log Service team for troubleshooting.

**Request failures and retries**

If you use an SDK to access Log Service, the access request may fail due to temporary network disconnection, transmission delay, or slow server response. These errors are thrown as exceptions. Log Service does not implement retry. When you use the SDK, you must customize the handling logic, for example, resend the request or report an error.

##### 3.2.1.4 API specifications

SDKs in different languages are implemented in different methods. However, all relevant API operations comply with the request-response principle. These API operations are called by using the following procedure:
1. Create a request instance by using request parameters.
2. Call the corresponding API operation in the SDK and pass the API information to the request
instance.
3. Encapsulate the results returned by the SDK interface into a response instance and then
return the response instance to the user. The following snippets show how to obtain the names of all Logstores in a project based on the preceding steps.

**Java**

```
// Other code... String accessId = "<youraccessId>"; // Specify your AccessKey ID. String accessKey = "<youraccessKey>"; // Specify your AccessKey secret. String project = "your_project"; // Specify your project name. String endpoint = "region_endpoint";// The China (Hangzhou) region is used as an exampl e. Specify the endpoint based on your region and access method. // Create a client instance. Client client = new Client(endpoint, accessId, accessKey); // Specify the project request parameter to initialize the ListLogstores request class. ListLogStoresRequest lsRequest = new ListLogStoresRequest(project); // Use the request instance to call the ListLogstores API operation. The returned param eter is the corresponding response instance. ListLogStoresResponse res = client.ListLogStores(lsRequest); // Access the response instance to retrieve the request results. ArrayList<String> names = res.GetLogStores(); // Other code...
```

**.NET(C#)**

```
// Other code... String accessId = "<youraccessId>"; // Specify your AccessKey ID. String accessKey = "<youraccessKey>"; // Specify your AccessKey secret. String project = "your_project"; // Specify your project name. String endpoint = "region_endpoint";// The China (Hangzhou) region is used as an exampl e. Specify the endpoint based on your region and access method. // Create a client instance. SLSClient client = new SLSClient(endpoint, accessId, accessKey); // Specify the project request parameter to initialize the ListLogstores request class. ListLogStoresRequest lsRequest = new ListLogStoresRequest(); lsRequest.Project = project; // Use the request instance to call the ListLogstores API operation. The returned param eter is the corresponding response instance. ListLogStoresResponse res = client.ListLogStores(lsRequest); // Access the response instance to retrieve the request results. List<String> names = res.Logstores; // Other code...
```

**PHP**

```
// Other code... $accessId = "<youraccessId>"; // Specify your AccessKey ID. $accessKey = "<youraccessKey>"; // Specify your AccessKey secret. $project = "your_project"; // Specify your project name. $endpoint = "region_endpoint";// The China (Hangzhou) region is used as an example. Spe cify the endpoint based on your region and access method. //Create a Log Service client instance. $client = new Aliyun_Sls_Client($endpoint, $accessId, $accessKey); // Specify the project request parameter to initialize the ListLogstores request class. $request = new Aliyun_Sls_Models_ListLogstoresRequest($project); // Use the request instance to call the ListLogstores API operation. The returned param eter is the corresponding response instance. $response = $client->listLogstores($request); // Access the response instance to retrieve the request results. $names = $response->getLogstores(); // Other code...
```

**Python**

```bash
// Other code... accessId = '<youraccessId>'; // Specify your AccessKey ID. accessKey = '<youraccessKey>'; // Specify your AccessKey secret. project = 'your_project'; // Specify your project name. endpoint = 'region_endpoint';// The China (Hangzhou) region is used as an example. Spec ify the endpoint based on your region and access method.
# Create a client instance.
client = LogClient(endpoint, accessId, accessKey)
# Specify the project request parameter to initialize the ListLogstores request class.
lsRequest = ListLogstoresRequest(project)
# Use the request instance to call the ListLogstores API operation. The returned parame
ter is the corresponding response instance. res = client.list_logstores(lsRequest)
# Access the response instance to retrieve the request results.
names = res.get_logstores(); // Other code...
```

The Log Service SDKs implement multiple API operations such as ListLogStores, and define the corresponding request and response classes. The Log Service SDKs of different languages also provide secondary APIs encapsulated with these basic request-response APIs. You do not need to create request instances or parse the content of the response. For more information about the secondary interfaces, see the API reference of each SDK.

#### 3.2.2 Java SDK

Log Service SDK for Java allows Java developers to perform operations in Log Service by using Java programs. You can use Maven dependencies to add the SDK. You can also download the SDK package to an on-premises server.

**Download URL**

Log Service SDK for Java supports J2SE V6.0 and later. Download the latest Java SDK for Log Service

**Step 1: Create an Apsara Stack tenant account**

To access Log Service, you must create an account in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Step 2: Obtain an Apsara Stack AccessKey pair**

To use Log Service SDK for Java, you must obtain an AccessKey pair. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. Select an AccessKey pair for the SDK. The AccessKey pair will be used in the following steps and must be kept confidential. For information about how to use an AccessKey pair in Log Service SDK for Java, see Basic configurations.

**Step 3: Create a project and a Logstore in the Log Service**

**console**

Use Log Service SDK for Java to create a project and a Logstore.

> **Note:** The account that you use to create the project and the Logstore must be the same as the account that you used to obtain the AccessKey pair.
> The project name must be unique in Log Service. The Logstore name must be unique in the project.
> After you create the project, you cannot modify its region or migrate the project across regions.

**Step 4: Install a Java development environment**

Log Service SDK for Java supports Java development environment J2SE V6.0 and later. You can visit the Java official website to download and install the Java development environment.

**Step 5: Install Log Service SDK for Java**

After you install the Java development environment, you must install Log Service SDK for Java. To install Log Service SDK for Java, use one of the following methods: Download the latest SDK for Java package from Apache Maven. Add the following configurations to your Maven project:

```xml
<dependency>
         <groupId>com.google.protobuf</groupId>
         <artifactId>protobuf-java</artifactId>
         <version>2.5.0</version>
</dependency> <dependency> <groupId>com.aliyun.openservices</groupId> <artifactId>aliyun-log</artifactId> <version>0.6.7</version> <exclusions>
        <exclusion>
            <groupId>com.google.protobuf</groupId>
            <artifactId>protobuf-java</artifactId>
       </exclusion>
</exclusions> </dependency>
```

Download Log Service SDK for Java package, and then reference the local package in your Java project.
1. Download Log Service SDK for Java package. Log Service SDK for Java is periodically
updated. You can use Maven to obtain the latest version.
2. Decompress the downloaded package to a specified directory. Log Service SDK for Java
does not require installation.
3. Add all JAR packages (including third-party dependent packages) in the SDK package to
your Java project. For more information, see the relevant documents about integrated development environment (IDE).

**Step 6: Start a new Java project**

The following sample code shows how to use Log Service SDK for Java. To interact with Log Service and obtain the relevant output, run the following sample code in a text editor or Java IDE:


**Usage notes**

To improve the I/O efficiency of your system, we recommend that you do not use SDKs to write data to Log Service. For information about the recommended data writing methods, see the "Producer Library" section in **User Guide**. **Producer Library** To call API operations for data consumption in Log Service, we recommend that you do not use SDKs. Log Service provides an advanced consumer library. The consumer library consumes data in a manner that is transparent to the user, and provides advanced features such as load balancing and sequential consumption. For more information, see Consumer Library in **User Guide**. **Consumer Library**

#### 3.2.3. .NET SDK

Log Service provides developers with Log Service SDK for .NET to simplify the use of Log Service.

**Download URL**

Log Service SDK for .NET allows developers on Windows to use Log Service on the .NET platform. Log Service SDK for .NET supports .NET Framework 3.5, .NET Framework 4.0, and .NET Framework 4.5. Even though different SDK files are used for different .NET Framework versions, the APIs and features of these versions are the same. The download URL of Log Service SDK for .NET is GitHub.

**Step 1: Create an Apsara Stack tenant account**

To access Log Service, you must create an account in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Step 2: Obtain an AccessKey pair**

To use Log Service SDK for .NET, you must obtain an AccessKey pair. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console and select an AccessKey pair for the SDK. The AccessKey pair will be used in the following steps and must be kept confidential. For information about how to use an AccessKey pair in Log Service SDK for .NET, see Basic configurations.

**Step 3: Create a project and a Logstore in the Log Service**

**console**

Use Log Service SDK for .NET to create a project and a Logstore.

> **Note:** The account that you use to create the project and the Logstore must be the same as the account that you used to obtain the AccessKey pair.
> The project name must be unique in Log Service. The Logstore name must be unique in the project.
> After you create the project, you cannot modify its region or migrate the project across regions.

**Step 4: Install a .NET development environment**

Log Service SDK for .NET supports the .NET Framework 3.5, .NET Framework 4.0, and .NET Framework 4.5 development environments. We recommend that you install one of the following .NET development environments: Microsoft .NET Framework 3.5, Microsoft .NET Framework 4.0, or Microsoft .NET Framework 4.5 (based on your environment) Visual Studio 2010 or later

**Step 5: Download and install Log Service SDK for .NET**

After you build a .NET development environment, you must install Log Service SDK for .NET. To install Log Service SDK for .NET, perform the following steps:
1. Download Log Service SDK for .NET.
Download the latest Log Service SDK for .NET from Github. Dwnload the old version of Log Service SDK for .NET package.
2. Decompress the downloaded package to a specified directory. Log Service SDK for .NET
does not require installation. The following step describes how to use the SDK in your Visual Studio project.

**Step 6: Create a Log Service .NET project**

After you install the .NET development environment and Log Service SDK for .NET, you can create a Log Service .NET project. For more information, see the LOG SDK Sample project in the SLS SDK 40 solution.

#### 3.2.4. .NET Core SDK

Log Service provides developers with Log Service SDK for .NET Core to simplify the use of Log Service.

**Background information**

Log Service SDK for .NET Core allows developers to use Log Service by using the .NET Core framework. The download URL of Log Service SDK for .NET Core, seeGitHub.

**Procedure**

1. Create an Apsara Stack tenant account.
To access Log Service, you must create an account in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. Obtain an Apsara Stack AccessKey pair.
To use Log Service SDK for .NET Core, you must obtain an Apsara Stack AccessKey pair. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console and select an AccessKey pair for the SDK. The AccessKey pair will be used in the following steps and must be kept confidential. For information about how to use the AccessKey pair in Log Service SDK for .NET Core, see Basic configurations.
3. Create a project and a Logstore.
Before you can use the SDK, you must create a project and a Logstore in the Log Service console.
1. Log on to the Log Service console.
2. In the Projects section, click **Create Project**.
3. Enter a **Project Name**, select a **Region**, and then click **OK**.
4. In the **Projects** section, click the name of the project. On the page that appears, click the
plus sign (**+**) in the left-side navigation pane. You can also click **Create** to create a Logstore as prompted after you create a project.
5. In the dialog box that appears, set the required parameters, and then click **OK**.
You must specify the Logstore name, data retention period, and number of shards. Set the number of shards based on your business requirements. In this example, four shards are created.

> **Note:** The account that you use to create the project and the Logstore must be the same as the account that you used to obtain the AccessKey pair.
> The project name must be unique in Log Service. The Logstore name must be unique in the project.
> After you create the project, you cannot modify its region or migrate the project across regions.

4. Install the .NET Core development environment.
Log Service SDK for .NET Core supports the following versions: .NET Core 2.0 .NET Framework (with .NET Core 1.x SDK) 4.6.2 .NET Framework (with .NET Core 2.0 SDK) 4.6.1 For more information about all supported versions, visit GitHub.
5. Download and install Log Service SDK for .NET Core.
After you build the .NET Core development environment, you must install Log Service SDK for .NET Core. i. Download Log Service SDK for .NET Core. ii. Decompress the downloaded package to a specified directory. Log Service SDK for .NET Core does not require installation. You can use Log Service SDK for .NET Core for your Visual Studio project.
6. Create a Log Service .NET Core project.
After you install the .NET Core development environment and Log Service SDK for .NET Core, you can create a .NET Core project. For more information, see GitHub Wiki.

#### 3.2.5 PHP SDK

Log Service provides developers with Log Service SDK for PHP to simplify the use of Log Service.

**Download URL**

You can download Log Service SDK for PHP from GitHub:

**Step 1: Create an Apsara Stack tenant account**

To access Log Service, you must create an account in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Step 2: Obtain an Apsara Stack AccessKey pair**

To use Log Service SDK for PHP, you must obtain an AccessKey pair. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. Select an AccessKey pair for the SDK. For information about how to use an AccessKey pair in Log Service SDK for PHP, see Basic configurations.

**Step 3: Create a project and a Logstore in the Log Service**

Log Service SDK for PHP supports PHP V5.2.1 and later. You can install a supported PHP on an on-premises server and build a PHP development environment.

#### 3.2.6 Python SDK

Log Service provides developers with Log Service SDK for Python to simplify the use of Log Service.

**Download URLs**

Download Log Service SDK for Python to . You can also download Log Service SDK for Python from GitHub: https://github.com/aliyun/aliyun-log-python-sdk

**Step 1: Create an Apsara Stack tenant account**

To access Log Service, you must create an account in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Step 2: Obtain an Apsara Stack AccessKey pair**

To use Log Service SDK for Python, you must obtain an AccessKey pair. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. Select an AccessKey pair for the SDK. The AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. The AccessKey pair will be used in the following steps and must be kept confidential. For information about how to use an AccessKey pair in Log Service SDK for Python, see Basic configurations.

**Step 3: Create a project and a Logstore in the Log Service**

**console**

Before you can use the SDK, you must create a project and a Logstore in the Log Service console.
1. Log on to the Log Service console.
2. In the Projects section, click **Create Project**.
3. Set the **Project Name** and the **Region** parameters, and then click **OK**.
4. In the **Projects** section, click the name of the project. On the page that appears, click the
plus sign (**+**) in the left-side navigation pane. You can also click **Create** to create a Logstore as prompted after you create a project.
5. In the dialog box that appears, set the required parameters, and then click **OK**.
You must specify the Logstore name, data retention period, and number of shards. Set the number of shards based on your business requirements. In this example, four shards are created.

> **Note:** The account that you use to create the project and the Logstore must be the same as the account that you used to obtain the AccessKey pair.
> The project name must be unique in Log Service. The Logstore name must be unique in the project.
> After you create the project, you cannot modify its region or migrate the project across regions.

**Step 4: Install the Python development environment**

Log Service SDK for Python is a pure Python library that supports all operating systems on which Python runs, such as Linux, Mac OS X, and Windows. To install the Python development environment, perform the following steps:
1. Download and install the latest Python installation package. For more informaton, see
Python installation package.

> **Note:** Log Service SDK for Python supports Python 2.6, 2.7, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, and 3.6. You can run the `python -V` command to check the current version of Python.
> Python no longer supports Python 2.6 or Python 3.3. We recommend that you use Python 2.7, Python 3.4, or a later version.

2. Download and install the Python package management tool pip. For more informaton, see
pip. After you install pip, run the `pip -V` command to check whether the installation is successful and view the pip version.

**Step 5: Install Log Service SDK for Python**

Run the following command as an administrator in Shell to install Log Service SDK for Python.

```
pip install -U aliyun-log-python-sdk
```

#### 3.2.8 SDK for C

The Log Service SDK for C is used to access logs in Log Service from multiple platforms, such as the MIPS and OpenWrt systems. The SDK for C uses libcurl as a network library. The apr/apr-util library resolves issues about memory management and cross-platform operations. You can use the SDK for C after you compile a small part of the source code. In addition, the C Producer Library and C Producer Lite Library provide you with a one-stop log collection solution across different platforms. This solution features simple deployment, high performance, and low resource consumption. For more information, visit the following GitHub URLs: C Producer Library (recommended for servers) C Producer Lite Library (recommended for IoT and smart devices)

Log Service provides developers with the SDK for Go to simplify the use of Log Service. var express = require('express') var morgan = require('morgan') var app = express() const logger = morgan(function (tokens, req, res) {

```
    tokens.status(req, res),
    tokens.res(req, res, 'content-length'), '-',
    tokens['response-time'](req, res), 'ms'
  ].join(' ')
```
